536	/**
537	 * The tool call's input line.
538	 *
539	 * **SYNTHESISED, and it has to be.** `ToolNode.inputPreview` is required and
540	 * {@link CodexToolCall} carries no input at all — it has `outputPreview` and no
541	 * counterpart. So this describes the CALL rather than quoting its arguments: the
542	 * namespaced tool name, plus a spawn's requested task name.
543	 *
544	 * The task name is safe to show and that is a measurement, not an assumption:
545	 * spec C7 records 17 of 17 spawn-bearing records carrying `task_name` in
546	 * plaintext against 24 of 24 `message` fields as ciphertext. The two fields
547	 * travel together and only one of them is opaque. The `message` bytes are not
548	 * on {@link CodexSpawn} at all — only their count is — so they cannot reach
549	 * here even by mistake.
550	 */
551	export function codexInputPreview(call: CodexToolCall, spawn: CodexSpawn | undefined): string {
552	  const namespace = optionalString(call.namespace);
553	  const name = namespace === null ? call.name : `${namespace}.${call.name}`;
554	  if (spawn === undefined) return name;
555	  const requested = spawn.requestedTaskName;
556	  return requested === null || requested === '' ? name : `${name} ${requested}`;
557	}

559	/**
560	 * `CodexToolCall` (+ its spawn, when it is one) -> `ToolNode`.
561	 *
562	 * `id` is the `call_id`, which the fingerprint guarantees is present
563	 * (`callIdMissing` refuses without one) and which is the same kind of thing
564	 * Claude Code's `tool_use id` is.
565	 *
566	 * **`itemId` does NOT survive into the node, and that is a known limitation.**
567	 * Spec C4's hook join resolves `tool_use_id` against the UNION of `call_id` and
568	 * `event_msg.payload.item.id`, and a shell command's item id is an unrelated
569	 * `exec-<uuid>`: 40 of 64 hook records resolve against `call_id` alone, 64
570	 * against the union. `ToolNode` has no second id field and this package may not
571	 * add one, so a hook join performed against `ToolNode.id` alone would drop
572	 * every shell call. `CodexToolCall.itemId` carries the other half and liveness
573	 * (DoD 2.5) must join through it, not through the tree.
574	 *
575	 * STATUS is derived, because {@link CodexToolCall} carries none. The output
576	 * record is this format's completion record — every completed call in the
577	 * corpus has a `function_call_output` or `custom_tool_call_output` — so its
578	 * absence is evidence of an unfinished call rather than a guess. A refused
579	 * spawn is `error`, which is DoD 2.4's "rendered as a failed call".
580	 */
581	export function toCodexToolNode(call: CodexToolCall, spawn: CodexSpawn | undefined): ToolNode {
582	  const refused = spawn !== undefined && spawn.refused;
583	  const status: ToolNode['status'] = refused
584	    ? 'error'
585	    : call.outputPreview === undefined
586	      ? 'running'
587	      : 'done';
588	  // A refused spawn's `refusalText` IS the engine's output for that call, so it
589	  // is what the result line shows. `outputPreview` is preferred when both
590	  // exist; they are the same bytes by construction.
591	  const result = call.outputPreview ?? (refused ? (spawn?.refusalText ?? undefined) : undefined);
592	  return {
593	    id: call.callId,
594	    toolName: call.name,
595	    status,
596	    inputPreview: codexInputPreview(call, spawn),
597	    ...(result === undefined ? {} : { resultPreview: result }),
598	    // OUR truncation is not the engine's. `outputTruncated` is Codex's own
599	    // claim about the payload it wrote, which is exactly what `ToolNode.
600	    // truncated` means; it crosses verbatim including `false`, because an
601	    // explicit "I did not truncate this" is a claim and is worth more than an
602	    // absence.
603	    ...(call.outputTruncated === undefined ? {} : { truncated: call.outputTruncated }),
604	  };
605	}

607	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
608	// The two-key join (spec C4 / C4a)
609	// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
610	
611	interface SpawnJoin {
612	  /** Child thread id -> the spawn that named it. */
613	  readonly childToSpawn: ReadonlyMap<string, CodexSpawn>;
614	  /** `call_id` -> the spawn made by that call. */
615	  readonly spawnByCallId: ReadonlyMap<string, CodexSpawn>;
616	  /** `call_id` -> the child thread id it resolved to. */
617	  readonly callToChild: ReadonlyMap<string, string>;
618	  /** Per-spawn resolution, in the golden's `child_resolved_by` vocabulary. */
619	  readonly joins: readonly CodexSpawnJoin[];
620	  readonly orphans: readonly { readonly spawn: CodexSpawn; readonly key: string }[];
621	  readonly refused: number;
622	  readonly resolved: number;
623	  readonly withoutOutputKey: number;
624	}
625	
626	/**
627	 * Resolve every spawn to its child, by whichever of the two keys the dialect
628	 * supplied (C4a).
629	 *
630	 * The keys are read from the spawn's OWN output and joined here against the
631	 * thread set. `CodexSpawn.childThreadId` and `childResolvedBy` are deliberately
632	 * NOT trusted: `parse.ts` sees one thread at a time and cannot know the other
633	 * threads' ids, so a value there would be someone else's join, and DoD 2.4
634	 * makes the join this module's.
635	 *
636	 * Order of the two keys is `task_name` first, then `agent_id`. They are never
637	 * both populated in one output on the corpus — a `v2` output is
638	 * `{"task_name": ...}` and a `v1` output is `{"agent_id": ..., "nickname": ...}`
639	 * — so the order decides nothing today and is fixed so it cannot decide
640	 * something silently tomorrow.
641	 */
642	function joinSpawns(
643	  spawns: readonly CodexSpawn[],
644	  threadsById: ReadonlyMap<string, CodexThread>,
645	  threadsByAgentPath: ReadonlyMap<string, CodexThread>,
646	): SpawnJoin {
647	  const childToSpawn = new Map<string, CodexSpawn>();
648	  const spawnByCallId = new Map<string, CodexSpawn>();
649	  const callToChild = new Map<string, string>();
650	  const joins: CodexSpawnJoin[] = [];
651	  const orphans: { spawn: CodexSpawn; key: string }[] = [];
652	  let refused = 0;
653	  let resolved = 0;
654	  let withoutOutputKey = 0;
655	
656	  for (const spawn of spawns) {
657	    spawnByCallId.set(spawn.callId, spawn);
658	
659	    // DoD 2.4. A refusal is a failed CALL, never a park: the engine declined,
660	    // it did not fail to join. It resolves to no child and it must not be
661	    // counted as an orphan either - there is no missing child to report.
662	    if (spawn.refused) {
663	      refused += 1;
664	      // `refused` IS A RESOLUTION, not a park and not an unresolved join. The
665	      // engine answered the call - it declined it - and that is a different
666	      // fact from a join that was attempted and found nothing. The golden's
667	      // own distribution over this corpus is 8 / 1 / 1 / 0 across the four
668	      // members, so `unresolved` is the one that fires zero times, not this.
669	      joins.push({ callId: spawn.callId, childThreadId: null, resolvedBy: 'refused' });
670	      continue;
671	    }
672	
673	    const taskName = spawn.outputTaskName;
674	    if (taskName !== null && taskName !== '') {
675	      const child = threadsByAgentPath.get(taskName);
676	      if (child !== undefined) {
677	        resolved += 1;
678	        childToSpawn.set(child.threadId, spawn);
679	        callToChild.set(spawn.callId, child.threadId);
680	        joins.push({
681	          callId: spawn.callId,
682	          childThreadId: child.threadId,
683	          resolvedBy: 'output_task_name_equals_agent_path',
684	        });
685	        continue;
686	      }
687	      orphans.push({ spawn, key: taskName });
688	      joins.push({ callId: spawn.callId, childThreadId: null, resolvedBy: 'unresolved' });
689	      continue;
690	    }
691	
692	    const agentId = spawn.outputAgentId;
693	    if (agentId !== null && agentId !== '') {
694	      const child = threadsById.get(agentId);
695	      if (child !== undefined) {
696	        resolved += 1;
697	        childToSpawn.set(child.threadId, spawn);
698	        callToChild.set(spawn.callId, child.threadId);
699	        joins.push({
700	          callId: spawn.callId,
701	          childThreadId: child.threadId,
702	          resolvedBy: 'output_agent_id_equals_thread_id',
703	        });
704	        continue;
705	      }
706	      orphans.push({ spawn, key: agentId });
707	      joins.push({ callId: spawn.callId, childThreadId: null, resolvedBy: 'unresolved' });
708	      continue;
709	    }
710	
711	    withoutOutputKey += 1;
712	    joins.push({ callId: spawn.callId, childThreadId: null, resolvedBy: 'unresolved' });
713	  }
714	
715	  return {
716	    childToSpawn,
717	    spawnByCallId,
718	    callToChild,
719	    joins,
720	    orphans,
721	    refused,
722	    resolved,
723	    withoutOutputKey,
724	  };
725	}

731	/**
732	 * Why this subagent cannot be attached, or `null` when it can.
733	 *
734	 * The order is normative and every step is a different fact:
735	 *
736	 *  1. `noAgentPath`      - the KEY is absent AND no spawn named this thread.
737	 *  2. `forkBoundaryMissing` - the C5 pair is half-declared.
738	 *  3. `dialectV1`        - the key is present-and-null AND no spawn named it.
739	 *                          TRIPWIRE, must fire zero times.
740	 *  4. `duplicateAgentPath` - a path already claimed. TRIPWIRE, engine-enforced.
741	 *  5. `parentAgentMissing` - `parent_thread_id` absent, or naming no thread.
742	 *
743	 * `parentNotGrafted` is the sixth and is NOT decided here: whether a child's
744	 * parent ended up in the tree is not knowable until the tree has been walked,
745	 * so it is applied afterwards, in {@link graftCodexThreads}.
746	 *
747	 * **`noAgentPath` CONSULTS THE SPAWNS, AND THE FIRST VERSION OF IT DID NOT.**
748	 * It returned on `!thread.agentPath.present` alone, and that parked EVERY v1
749	 * subagent: the top-level `session_meta.payload.agent_path` key is ABSENT on a
750	 * v1 thread (the present-and-`null` field is the NESTED
751	 * `source.subagent.thread_spawn.agent_path`, which is a different field).
752	 * Measured on `resume-twice-v1`: the spawn join resolved the child correctly
753	 * as `output_agent_id_equals_thread_id`, and this function threw the result
754	 * away one line later — 0 spawn edges, 1 park, a tree containing only
755	 * `/root`. That is the ruling the user REVERSED on corrected evidence in
756	 * Phase 1, reintroduced through a third door, and the park's own `reason`
757	 * string described the correct behaviour while the code did the opposite.
758	 *
759	 * Absence of the top-level key is the NORMAL state of a v1 subagent and of
760	 * every root thread. It is the v2 join key and v2's alone. **Whether a thread
761	 * is joinable is answered by asking the SPAWNS**, never by this field.
762	 * `noAgentPath` keeps a real population — a thread no spawn names by either
763	 * key — and that is what it now means.
764	 *
765	 * `dialectV1` is checked BEFORE placement on purpose. A keyless child with a
766	 * good `parent_thread_id` could be placed, and placing it would make the
767	 * tripwire unreachable — which is the whole failure mode a tripwire exists to
768	 * prevent. The check is about the KEY, not about whether we happened to manage.
769	 */
770	function parkCodeFor(
771	  thread: CodexThread,
772	  namedBySpawn: boolean,
773	  duplicatePath: boolean,
774	  threadsById: ReadonlyMap<string, CodexThread>,
775	): CodexParkCode | null {
776	  // ABSENCE OF THE TOP-LEVEL KEY IS NOT A REASON TO PARK, and reading it as
777	  // one parked every v1 subagent in existence. See the doc block above.
778	  if (!thread.agentPath.present && !namedBySpawn) return 'noAgentPath';
779	
780	  const forkedFrom = thread.forkedFromId.present;
781	  const forkStart = thread.subagentHistoryStartOrdinal.present;
782	  if (forkedFrom !== forkStart) return 'forkBoundaryMissing';
783	
784	  const path = optionalString(thread.agentPath);
785	  if (path === null && !namedBySpawn) return 'dialectV1';
786	
787	  if (duplicatePath) return 'duplicateAgentPath';
788	
789	  const parentId = optionalString(thread.parentThreadId);
790	  if (parentId === null || !threadsById.has(parentId)) return 'parentAgentMissing';
791	
792	  return null;
793	}

796	// Assembly

798	
799	interface SessionBuild {
800	  readonly root: CodexThread;
801	  readonly childrenOf: ReadonlyMap<string, readonly CodexThread[]>;
802	  readonly join: SpawnJoin;
803	  readonly spawnEdges: SpawnEdge[];
804	  readonly parked: ParkedGraft[];
805	  readonly depthDisagreements: CodexDepthDisagreement[];
806	  readonly agentsWithoutSpawnEdgeRef: { count: number };
807	  /**
808	   * Every thread this walk actually placed in the tree.
809	   *
810	   * A thread can be attachable and still be unreachable: if its own parent
811	   * parked, the parent is not in `childrenOf` and the recursion never descends
812	   * to it. Without this set that thread would be SILENTLY DROPPED - present in
813	   * neither `root` nor `parked` - which is precisely the failure the park
814	   * vocabulary exists to make visible. The caller parks the remainder.
815	   */
816	  readonly visited: Set<string>;
817	}

819	/**
820	 * The depth this node reports, and it is the RECORDED one.
821	 *
822	 * DoD 2.4: "depth-2 fixture yields `depth` from the transcript, not
823	 * recomputed." So `source.subagent.thread_spawn.depth` is what is emitted, on
824	 * both {@link SpawnEdge.depth} and {@link AgentNode.spawnDepth}.
825	 *
826	 * The walked depth is still computed, and a disagreement is RECORDED rather
827	 * than silently resolved — {@link CodexGraftResult.depthDisagreements}. The
828	 * Claude Code `SpawnEdge` already carries this pair for the same reason: a
829	 * recorded value can contradict a walked one, and the contradiction is
830	 * information.
831	 *
832	 * When no depth was recorded the walked one is used and the pair is not a
833	 * disagreement — there is nothing to disagree with.
834	 */
835	function depthFor(thread: CodexThread, walked: number, build: SessionBuild): number {
836	  const recorded = thread.spawnDepth.present && typeof thread.spawnDepth.value === 'number'
837	    ? thread.spawnDepth.value
838	    : null;
839	  if (recorded === null) return walked;
840	  if (recorded !== walked) {
841	    build.depthDisagreements.push({ threadId: thread.threadId, recorded, walked });
842	  }
843	  return recorded;
844	}
845	
846	function buildAgent(thread: CodexThread, walkedDepth: number, build: SessionBuild): AgentNode {
847	  build.visited.add(thread.threadId);
848	  const isRoot = thread.threadId === build.root.threadId;
849	  const nodeId = isRoot ? 'root' : thread.threadId;
850	  const depth = isRoot ? 0 : depthFor(thread, walkedDepth, build);
851	
852	  // Tool calls in transcript order. `ordinal` is documented as dense and
853	  // monotonic from 0 per thread, so it is a total order within a thread and no
854	  // tie-break is needed; the id is compared anyway so the sort is stable across
855	  // engines that might not honour that.
856	  const calls = [...thread.toolCalls].sort((a, b) =>
857	    a.ordinal !== b.ordinal ? a.ordinal - b.ordinal : a.callId < b.callId ? -1 : a.callId > b.callId ? 1 : 0,
858	  );
859	
860	  const childThreads = build.childrenOf.get(thread.threadId) ?? [];
861	  const placed = new Set<string>();
862	  const children: TreeNode[] = [];
863	
864	  for (const call of calls) {
865	    const spawn = build.join.spawnByCallId.get(call.callId);
866	    children.push(toCodexToolNode(call, spawn));
867	    if (spawn === undefined) continue;
868	
869	    const childId = build.join.callToChild.get(call.callId);
870	    if (childId === undefined) continue;
871	    const child = childThreads.find((c) => c.threadId === childId);
872	    if (child === undefined) continue;
873	
874	    // The node is built FIRST and the edge takes its depth off the node. Calling
875	    // `depthFor` here as well would record any recorded/walked disagreement
876	    // twice for one thread - a double count in the very diagnostic whose job is
877	    // to say how often the two disagree.
878	    const childNode = buildAgent(child, depth + 1, build);
879	    placed.add(child.threadId);
880	    build.spawnEdges.push({
881	      // Spec C4's hook/transcript id. `call_id` is always present.
882	      toolUseId: call.callId,
883	      agentId: child.threadId,
884	      parentNodeId: nodeId,
885	      // DoD 2.4: the transcript's depth, not the walked one. `AgentNode.
886	      // spawnDepth` already holds it, so the two can never disagree.
887	      depth: childNode.spawnDepth,
888	      recordedDepth: childNode.spawnDepth,
889	    });
890	    // A subagent `AgentNode` sits BESIDE the tool call that spawned it, never
891	    // inside it: `ToolNode` has no `children` field and that stays true. The
892	    // real spawn relationship exists only in `spawnEdges`.
893	    children.push(childNode);
894	  }
895	
896	  // Children whose spawning call could not be identified. They are still this
897	  // thread's children - `parent_thread_id` is a primary key and spec C4 prefers
898	  // it - so they are placed, after the calls, with NO `SpawnEdge`. Counted, not
899	  // silent: what is missing is the filament, not the agent.
900	  for (const child of childThreads) {
901	    if (placed.has(child.threadId)) continue;
902	    build.agentsWithoutSpawnEdgeRef.count += 1;
903	    children.push(buildAgent(child, depth + 1, build));
904	  }
905	
906	  const status: AgentNode['status'] = children.some(
907	    (node) => 'toolName' in node && node.status === 'running',
908	  )
909	    ? 'running'
910	    : 'done';
911	
912	  const contextNow = thread.contextNow;
913	  const burn = thread.burn;
914	
915	  return {
916	    id: nodeId,
917	    kind: isRoot ? 'main' : 'subagent',
918	    label: codexNodeLabel(thread, isRoot),
919	    status,
920	    spawnDepth: depth,
921	    children,
922	    // Absent stays absent. A zero here would claim an empty context window,
923	    // which is a wrong number rather than a missing one.
924	    ...(contextNow === undefined ? {} : { contextNow }),
925	    ...(burn === undefined ? {} : { burn }),
926	    // `session_meta`'s own timestamp at ordinal 0, never `mtimeMs` — see the
927	    // note beside {@link CodexGraftOptions}.
928	    startedAt: thread.startedAtMs,
929	    // `mtimeMs` is the last write to the transcript, which for a thread that is
930	    // not running IS when it stopped changing - the same reasoning the OpenCode
931	    // grafter applies to `time_updated`. A running agent has no end and the KEY
932	    // IS OMITTED rather than set to `undefined`.
933	    ...(status === 'running' ? {} : { endedAt: thread.mtimeMs }),
934	  };
935	}

940	function addTokens(a: TokenPair, b: TokenPair): TokenPair {
941	  return { prompt: a.prompt + b.prompt, output: a.output + b.output };

944	/**
945	 * Build one `SessionState` per ROOT thread, with every descendant grafted in.
946	 *
947	 * A subagent is an `AgentNode` INSIDE its root's session, never a deck entry of
948	 * its own — the same shape both other engines produce.
949	 *
950	 * @throws never. G3: a refusal is carried, not thrown, and malformed input is
951	 * counted and skipped. Every condition that would be an exception elsewhere is
952	 * a counter or a park entry on {@link CodexGraftResult}.
953	 */
954	export function graftCodexThreads(input: CodexGraftInput): CodexGraftResult {
955	  const { threads } = input;
956	  const livenessFor = input.options?.livenessFor ?? defaultCodexLiveness;
957	  const workspaceMatch = input.options?.workspaceMatch ?? defaultCodexWorkspaceMatch;
958	  const projectSlug = input.options?.projectSlug ?? defaultCodexProjectSlug;
959	
960	  // ---- indexes -----------------------------------------------------------
961	  const threadsById = new Map<string, CodexThread>();
962	  for (const thread of threads) {
963	    // First declaration wins. A thread id repeated in the input is the fork
964	    // boundary arriving un-deduplicated (spec C5: a forked child re-serialises
965	    // a second `session_meta`, so a thread can be DECLARED in more than one
966	    // file); `owningFile` is the file whose ordinal-0 meta declares it and
967	    // `parse.ts` is what applies that rule. Taking the first keeps this module
968	    // from silently preferring a later, inherited copy.
969	    if (!threadsById.has(thread.threadId)) threadsById.set(thread.threadId, thread);
970	  }
971	
972	  const allSpawns: CodexSpawn[] = [];
973	  for (const thread of threads) for (const spawn of thread.spawns) allSpawns.push(spawn);
974	
975	  // `agent_path` -> thread, for the v2 key. Built over threads that HOLD a
976	  // path; a duplicate is the `duplicateAgentPath` tripwire and the first wins.
977	  const threadsByAgentPath = new Map<string, CodexThread>();
978	  const claimedPaths = new Set<string>();
979	  const duplicatePathThreads = new Set<string>();
980	  for (const thread of threadsById.values()) {
981	    const path = optionalString(thread.agentPath);
982	    if (path === null) continue;
983	    if (claimedPaths.has(path)) {
984	      duplicatePathThreads.add(thread.threadId);
985	      continue;
986	    }
987	    claimedPaths.add(path);
988	    threadsByAgentPath.set(path, thread);
989	  }
990	
991	  const join = joinSpawns(allSpawns, threadsById, threadsByAgentPath);
992	
993	  // ---- session grouping (relation 1) --------------------------------------
994	  const bySession = new Map<string, CodexThread[]>();
995	  for (const thread of threadsById.values()) {
996	    const list = bySession.get(thread.sessionId) ?? [];
997	    list.push(thread);
998	    bySession.set(thread.sessionId, list);
999	  }
1000	
1001	  const sessions: SessionState[] = [];
1002	  const sessionsWithoutRootThread: string[] = [];
1003	  const rootIdentityDisagreements: string[] = [];
1004	  const depthDisagreements: CodexDepthDisagreement[] = [];
1005	  const spawnParentDisagreements: CodexSpawnParentDisagreement[] = [];
1006	  const agentsWithoutSpawnEdgeRef = { count: 0 };
1007	  let counters = emptyCounters();
1008	  let spawnsOrphaned = 0;
1009	
1010	  for (const thread of threadsById.values()) {
1011	    counters = addCounters(counters, thread.counters);
1012	    const looksRootById = thread.threadId === thread.sessionId;
1013	    const looksRootBySource = thread.threadSource === 'user';
1014	    if (looksRootById !== looksRootBySource) rootIdentityDisagreements.push(thread.threadId);
1015	  }
1016	
1017	  // Cross-assert the spawning call's thread against the child's own parent.
1018	  for (const [childId, spawn] of join.childToSpawn) {
1019	    const child = threadsById.get(childId);
1020	    if (child === undefined) continue;
1021	    const parentId = optionalString(child.parentThreadId);
1022	    if (parentId === spawn.threadId) continue;
1023	    spawnParentDisagreements.push({
1024	      childThreadId: childId,
1025	      spawningThreadId: spawn.threadId,
1026	      parentThreadId: parentId,
1027	    });
1028	  }
1029	
1030	  for (const [sessionId, group] of bySession) {
1031	    const root = group.find((t) => t.threadId === sessionId);
1032	    if (root === undefined) {
1033	      sessionsWithoutRootThread.push(sessionId);
1034	      continue;
1035	    }
1036	
1037	    const parked: ParkedGraft[] = [];
1038	    const attachable: CodexThread[] = [];
1039	
1040	    for (const thread of group) {
1041	      if (thread.threadId === root.threadId) continue;
1042	      const namedBySpawn = join.childToSpawn.has(thread.threadId);
1043	      const code = parkCodeFor(
1044	        thread,
1045	        namedBySpawn,
1046	        duplicatePathThreads.has(thread.threadId),
1047	        threadsById,
1048	      );
1049	      if (code === null) {
1050	        attachable.push(thread);
1051	        continue;
1052	      }
1053	      const spawn = join.childToSpawn.get(thread.threadId);
1054	      parked.push({
1055	        agentId: thread.threadId,
1056	        code,
1057	        ...(spawn === undefined ? {} : { toolUseId: spawn.callId }),
1058	        reason: CODEX_PARK_REASONS[code],
1059	        ...(optionalString(thread.parentThreadId) === null
1060	          ? {}
1061	          : { parentAgentId: optionalString(thread.parentThreadId) as string }),
1062	      });
1063	    }
1064	
1065	    // A spawn naming a child the corpus does not contain. Parked on the session
1066	    // the SPAWNING thread belongs to, keyed on the name the spawn used - there
1067	    // is no thread id to key on, which is the entire content of the case.
1068	    for (const orphan of join.orphans) {
1069	      const owner = threadsById.get(orphan.spawn.threadId);
1070	      if (owner === undefined || owner.sessionId !== sessionId) continue;
1071	      spawnsOrphaned += 1;
1072	      parked.push({
1073	        agentId: orphan.key,
1074	        code: 'orphanSpawn',
1075	        toolUseId: orphan.spawn.callId,
1076	        reason: CODEX_PARK_REASONS.orphanSpawn,
1077	      });
1078	    }
1079	
1080	    const childrenOf = new Map<string, CodexThread[]>();
1081	    for (const thread of attachable) {
1082	      const parentId = optionalString(thread.parentThreadId);
1083	      if (parentId === null) continue;
1084	      const list = childrenOf.get(parentId) ?? [];
1085	      list.push(thread);
1086	      childrenOf.set(parentId, list);
1087	    }
1088	
1089	    const spawnEdges: SpawnEdge[] = [];
1090	    const build: SessionBuild = {
1091	      root,
1092	      childrenOf,
1093	      join,
1094	      spawnEdges,
1095	      parked,
1096	      depthDisagreements,
1097	      agentsWithoutSpawnEdgeRef,
1098	      visited: new Set<string>(),
1099	    };
1100	    const rootNode = buildAgent(root, 0, build);
1101	
1102	    // A thread that passed every park check and is still not in the tree: its
1103	    // own parent parked, so the chain to the root is broken. This is exactly
1104	    // what the Claude Code grafter calls `parentNotGrafted`, and the webview
1105	    // already renders it - the reason lives one level up, at the parent's own
1106	    // park entry, which is why it is a different code from `parentAgentMissing`
1107	    // rather than a second use of it.
1108	    for (const thread of attachable) {
1109	      if (build.visited.has(thread.threadId)) continue;
1110	      const spawn = join.childToSpawn.get(thread.threadId);
1111	      parked.push({
1112	        agentId: thread.threadId,
1113	        code: 'parentNotGrafted',
1114	        ...(spawn === undefined ? {} : { toolUseId: spawn.callId }),
1115	        reason: CODEX_PARK_REASONS.parentNotGrafted,
1116	        ...(optionalString(thread.parentThreadId) === null
1117	          ? {}
1118	          : { parentAgentId: optionalString(thread.parentThreadId) as string }),
1119	      });
1120	    }
1121	
1122	    // `burn` is the session's spend, summed over every agent in the tree -
1123	    // `SessionState.burn`'s own contract. Parked agents contribute nothing,
1124	    // which falls out of walking `attachable`. A session where NO thread
1125	    // reports one leaves the key ABSENT rather than emitting a zero pair.
1126	    let burn: TokenPair | undefined;
1127	    const walk = (thread: CodexThread): void => {
1128	      if (thread.burn !== undefined) burn = burn === undefined ? thread.burn : addTokens(burn, thread.burn);
1129	      for (const child of childrenOf.get(thread.threadId) ?? []) walk(child);
1130	    };
1131	    walk(root);
1132	
1133	    const windowTokens = root.modelContextWindow;
1134	
1135	    sessions.push({
1136	      sessionId: root.threadId,
1137	      projectSlug: projectSlug(root),
1138	      // C11: written rather than left to the `'cc'` default, which is what
1139	      // makes G2's cross-engine isolation assertable at all.
1140	      engine: 'codex',
1141	      workspaceMatch: workspaceMatch(root),
1142	      liveness: livenessFor(root),
1143	      // Refusal is `fingerprint.ts`'s (G3, DoD 2.2). A thread that reaches here
1144	      // was accepted, so the grafter has no refusal of its own to express.
1145	      schemaOk: true,
1146	      // There is no cost figure anywhere in a Codex transcript and there is no
1147	      // price table in this repository. `0` here means NOT YET COMPUTED, which
1148	      // is what the field documents; it never means "free".
1149	      totals: { costUsd: 0 },
1150	      // The session's context LEVEL is the main transcript's, not the deepest
1151	      // subagent's: each thread has its own window. Absent stays absent.
1152	      ...(root.contextNow === undefined ? {} : { contextNow: root.contextNow }),
1153	      ...(burn === undefined ? {} : { burn }),
1154	      // DoD 2.6 / spec C8. `model_context_window` from the transcript and from
1155	      // nowhere else - Codex's network-fetched model cache states a different
1156	      // figure for what looks like the same concept and is on the G10
1157	      // never-opened list. ABSENT -> the key is omitted, never `0`.
1158	      //
1159	      // The cache is NOT NAMED here, and the omission is load-bearing:
1160	      // `never-open.ts` is the one file under `src/codex/` allowed to write
1161	      // those filenames, and `never-open.test.ts` greps every sibling and
1162	      // asserts each name appears only there. Writing the literal turned that
1163	      // test red - which is the guard working, on a comment, exactly as
1164	      // designed.
1165	      ...(windowTokens === undefined ? {} : { windowTokens }),
1166	      spawnEdges,
1167	      parked,
1168	      root: rootNode,
1169	    });
1170	  }
1171	
1172	  return {
1173	    sessions,
1174	    counters,
1175	    spawnsRefused: join.refused,
1176	    spawnsResolved: join.resolved,
1177	    spawnsOrphaned,
1178	    spawnsWithoutOutputKey: join.withoutOutputKey,
1179	    spawnJoins: join.joins,
1180	    agentsWithoutSpawnEdge: agentsWithoutSpawnEdgeRef.count,
1181	    depthDisagreements,
1182	    spawnParentDisagreements,
1183	    sessionsWithoutRootThread,
1184	    rootIdentityDisagreements,
1185	  };
1186	}
1187
